title: Until Powerhouse supports Artifact edits, Pattern governance runs on forum posts and a GitHub pull request
content:
Two "Short-Term Transitionary Measures" sections concede that the specified system does not yet exist. On the input side (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1), holders may submit by posting to the Sky Forum with "Pattern Artifact Edit Proposal" in the title, and "the post must include cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage" of supply. On the output side (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5.1), the Facilitator "works with the Core Facilitator to update the Atlas GitHub repository... to reflect proposals approved by Prime Governance."

The interesting substitution is on the input side: where Powerhouse would verify eligibility automatically, the interim rule reproduces the *guarantee* with a signature rather than dropping it. Eligibility remains cryptographically checkable by any reader; only the automation is missing.

The output side has no such equivalence. Applying an approved edit becomes a manual, two-person act in a Git repository — introducing a step where the recorded Artifact can diverge from what governance actually approved, and adding the Core Facilitator as a de facto participant in Pattern's amendment path even though no Pattern vote selects them.

The general lesson is that transitional measures are not uniformly faithful: some preserve the property they stand in for, and some quietly relocate trust. Reading them as a set shows which guarantees are currently real and which are procedural promises.
description: Proposals need cryptographic proof of holdings inside a titled forum post, and approved edits are applied by the Operational Facilitator working with the Core Facilitator on the Atlas repository.
